headline: LLM agents grounded in raw single-cell data for annotation and perturbation prediction
label: Grounded Llm Agents Single Cell
summary: Recent preprints couple LLM reasoning to explicit data and tools for scRNA-seq annotation, perturbation prediction and public metadata curation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is coupling LLM reasoning to explicit biological data and tools rather than parametric knowledge alone. scPilot grounds an LLM in raw scRNA-seq data and bioinformatics tools for step-by-step reasoning on annotation, trajectories and TF targeting. CellMaster applies an LLM-based agent to zero-shot scRNA-seq cell-type annotation, reporting 7.1% accuracy gains over CellTypist and scTab across 9 datasets. MechPert aggregates proposals from multiple LLM agents via consensus to predict unseen Perturb-seq responses, improving low-data Pearson scores. ChatDIA and the GEO metadata curation study apply zero-shot or open-weight LLM workflows to proteomics and public database metadata, outside single-cell analysis. What is new is less the agentic pattern itself than its anchoring to raw data and standardized analysis tools.
